questions.question_text: Under SC law, a BIC's supervisory authority over affiliated licensees can be delegated to:
questions.correct_answer: No one — BIC authority cannot be delegated
distractors: A senior associate with 5+ years experience
An office manager with a PM license
Any licensed broker within the firm
questions.explanation: The broker-in-charge designation cannot be assigned or delegated to another licensee (S.C. Code 40-57-30). Supervisory responsibility may not be handed to a team leader or team member either (S.C. Code 40-57-360).

questions.question_text: Which document is the BIC required to maintain under SC state law?
distractors: A daily transaction log
A quarterly financial report for LLR
A client satisfaction survey record
questions.explanation: The BIC must establish and maintain a written office policy and keep it readily accessible to supervised licensees (S.C. Code 40-57-135(A)). The policy has to describe the brokerage relationships the firm offers.

questions.question_text: Under the 2024 Practice Act, an associate may be affiliated with how many BICs?
distractors: Up to two BICs
As many BICs as they choose
One per office location
questions.explanation: An active broker or associate may not be licensed with more than one broker-in-charge at the same time (S.C. Code 40-57-330(B)). The BIC handles day-to-day supervision, trust accounts, and compliance.

questions.question_text: A seller rejects an offer outright without countering. What must the licensee give the offeror, and how quickly?
questions.correct_answer: A commission offer rejection form within 48 hours
distractors: A written explanation within 10 days
Nothing — only counteroffers must be documented
A copy of the seller's written rejection at closing
questions.explanation: When an offer is rejected without a counter, the licensee must give the offeror the commission's offer rejection form, signed to affirm the offer was presented, within forty-eight hours (S.C. Code 40-57-135(I)).

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a required duty of the BIC?
questions.correct_answer: Reviewing forms used by affiliated licensees
distractors: Personally attending all property showings
Approving all buyer mortgage applications
Conducting weekly team sales meetings
questions.explanation: BIC duties include reviewing and approving forms, supervising trust accounts, maintaining contact with licensees, instructing on trust fund handling, and being reasonably available to the public.

questions.question_text: A PMIC's role is most similar to which other position in SC real estate?
distractors: An appraiser for rental properties
A title attorney for lease closings
A mortgage broker for rental investors
questions.explanation: The PMIC supervises affiliated property managers, maintains PM trust accounts, and ensures compliance — similar to how a BIC supervises sales operations. SC's separate PM license category makes this a distinct role.

questions.question_text: A PMIC collects security deposits from tenants. Where must these funds be held?
distractors: In the property owner's personal account
In the PMIC's personal savings account
In the brokerage's operating account
questions.explanation: Security deposits and advance rental deposits are trust funds and must be held in the PM trust account. The PMIC is responsible for ensuring compliance with trust account rules.

questions.question_text: A property management company handles both sales and rentals. What is the best practice for trust accounts?
distractors: One combined trust account is sufficient
Three accounts: sales, rental, and reserves
No trust account needed for rental operations
questions.explanation: Best practice is two trust accounts: one for sales earnest money and one for rental security deposits and advance rent. The deposit deadlines differ, since sales checks turn on written acceptance and lease checks on lease signing.

questions.question_text: What additional requirement must a PMIC fulfill beyond holding a property manager license?
distractors: Hold a broker license for 2 years
Complete 60 hours of additional education
Obtain a separate PMIC exam certification
questions.explanation: A PMIC must hold an active property manager license and complete seven hours of approved instruction in property management accounting and record-keeping (S.C. Code 40-57-510(C)). There is no separate PMIC exam.

questions.question_text: A PMIC manages 50 rental units across 3 property owners. What bookkeeping requirement applies?
questions.correct_answer: Maintain a separate owner's ledger for each owner
distractors: One combined ledger for all units is sufficient
Only a single bank statement is required
Separate ledgers only for owners with 10+ units
questions.explanation: The PMIC must maintain an owner's ledger showing receipts and disbursements for each owner's properties, plus a tenant's ledger for each tenant. This applies regardless of the number of units per owner.

questions.question_text: An associate receives a $3,000 earnest money check on a Thursday. By when must the associate deliver it to the BIC?
distractors: Within 48 hours of receipt
Within 72 hours of receipt
At the next weekly office meeting
questions.explanation: Trust funds received by a licensee must reach the BIC or PMIC no later than the following business day (S.C. Code 40-57-136(B)). The BIC then deposits a check within 48 hours of written acceptance.

questions.question_text: A licensee is selling a rental property she owns personally. How must she reveal her license status?
questions.correct_answer: In bold, underlined capital letters on the first page of the contract
distractors: Verbally at the closing table
In a separate letter delivered after the contract is signed
Only if the buyer asks whether she is licensed
questions.explanation: A licensee in a personal transaction must reveal license status at first substantive contact, in any advertising, and in bold, underlined capital letters on the first page of the contract (S.C. Code 40-57-135(F)).

questions.question_text: A buyer makes a verbal offer through an SC associate. What must the associate do?
distractors: Present it verbally to the listing agent
Decline to present verbal offers
Record it in the office phone log
questions.explanation: SC licensees must reduce all offers, acceptances, and changes to writing. Verbal offers should be put in written form before presentation to ensure proper documentation.

questions.question_text: An SC brokerage firm operates under a national franchise name. What must its advertising reveal?
questions.correct_answer: The identity of the franchisee or trade name holder
distractors: The franchise's annual revenue
The franchise fee structure
The date the franchise agreement was signed
questions.explanation: When a firm operates under a trade or franchise name, the identity of the franchisee or trade name holder must be clearly revealed (S.C. Code 40-57-135(E)). The brand name by itself is not enough.

questions.question_text: Under the 2024 team advertising rules (effective May 2027), a team name must include which word?
distractors: Group
Associates
Partners
questions.explanation: Team names must end in the form '[team name] team at [brokerage firm]' (S.C. Code 40-57-360(E)). That rule takes effect May 15, 2027, giving teams three years from the 2024 Practice Act to comply.
